function: Primal-dual SAC jointly learns user scheduling, UAV trajectories, and transmit power of UAV base stations and jammers to maximize worst-case secrecy rate. p. 5-6.
system: UAV BSs (3) and jammers (2), 20 single-antenna users, 3+4 eavesdroppers, 1 km square; UAV antennas and band not stated; no RIS. p. 3, 10.
method: Primal-dual soft actor-critic (reward and cost critics, actor updating dual variable), constrained MDP, deep reinforcement learning; four-layer 128-neuron fully connected networks. p. 5-6, 9.
data_channel: Own simulator: line-of-sight gain g0 d^-2, g0 = -60 dB; random users and eavesdroppers in a 1 km square; no 3GPP or measured channel. p. 4, 9.
test_conditions: Same simulated area; separate training per number of jammers and eavesdroppers, then inference with the stored actor; learning-rate sweep. p. 9-10.
baselines: Learned: SAC (cost-penalty reward) and TD3. Non-learned: random method and greedy method (maximum power, nearest-UAV scheduling, random trajectory). p. 7-8.
metrics: Cumulative discount reward, average (worst-case) secrecy rate versus time slot, jammers and eavesdroppers, training convergence speed, learning-rate sensitivity, trajectory plot. p. 8-10.
complexity: none; the paper gives no operations count, parameter count or runtime, only the network layout (four layers, 128 hidden neurons). p. 9.
openness: none; no code or data link, simulation only. p. 9.
q1_support: p. 4: "are the line-of-sight links in our considered scenario" - own free-space model g = g0 d^-2 (p. 4), g0 = -60 dB (p. 9); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 10: "we store the parameters of the respective actor network after each algorithm training is completed" - training curves per number of jammers (Fig. 8a) and eavesdroppers (Fig. 9a); no model is tested on a setting it was not trained for.
q3_support: p. 7: "other DRL solutions namely SAC algorithm and TD3 algorithm to compare with the proposed primal-dual SAC algorithm"; random and greedy methods are the non-learned baselines; all compared on average secrecy rate (Figs. 8b, 9b, p. 9).
q4_support: p. 9: "are four-layer fully connected networks, and the number of neurons in their hidden layer is 128" - architecture only; no parameter count, operation count, complexity order or runtime for the proposed method.
q5_support: p. 9: "The experiments are simulated using Python v3.7 and the deep learning framework is Pytorch" - own simulation; no code or data link and no public dataset.
notes: Included under the aerial-link rule: the policy learns transmit power of UAV base stations and jammers (physical layer) jointly with user scheduling and trajectory (above physical layer), p. 5. Area 6 chosen (resource and power control of aerial links); the objective is a secrecy rate (physical-layer security with friendly jamming), which the areas do not name, so the reviewer may confirm that it is area 6 and not an excluded function. Users are single-antenna, admitted for area 6. q3 is 1 through TD3 and the random and greedy methods; SAC is close to an ablation of the primal-dual SAC and is not relied on. Figures read from page images of pages 8 and 9.
